title: No insurance?
message: Free adult medical care. Call RotaCare to ask about an appointment.
details: For uninsured Monterey Peninsula residents age 18 or older. Call 831-333-6495 to discuss your needs and arrange an appointment. The clinic lists limited in-person and telehealth sessions, plus Spanish interpreters. It does not offer dental or mental-health services. Confirm that the clinic can provide the care you need; appointments are not guaranteed.
evidence: Provider confirms free clinic, uninsured adult service area, appointment phone, interpreters and excluded services. No claim of same-day access.

title: Ready for recovery?
message: Ask CHS about substance-use treatment in Salinas or Monterey.
details: CHS offers outpatient substance-use treatment and assessments. Call Salinas at 831-237-7222 or Monterey at 831-383-7800 to start with an assessment. The provider accepts Medi-Cal and lists a sliding fee for private-pay clients. Confirm eligibility, costs and appointment availability directly; the page gives inconsistent adult/adolescent age language, so no age cutoff is asserted here.
evidence: Read treatment page and https://chservices.org/contact/. Both list the same outpatient numbers. Conflicting age wording excluded; no immediate treatment slot promised.

title: Energy bill piling up?
message: Ask Central Coast Energy Services about HEAP assistance.
details: Income-qualified households can request a HEAP application at 888-728-3637. Prepare a recent energy bill, household income records and the identification described in the application. If shutoff is threatened, contact your utility about payment arrangements and ask CCES for current emergency-assistance locations. Approval and available funding must be confirmed.
evidence: Provider FAQ describes service counties, income screening, application phone, documents and shutoff guidance.

title: A warmer home.
message: Ask about free home weatherization for eligible households.
details: CCES lists weatherization for qualifying households. Owners and renters may apply; renters need the property owner to sign the service agreement too. Call 888-728-3637 to ask about eligibility, assessment and current availability. This is an inquiry about the program, not a promised repair or installation.
evidence: Provider FAQ confirms weatherization applications by owners/renters and the owner-signature requirement.

title: Medicare questions?
message: Free, unbiased guidance from Alliance on Aging.
details: HICAP helps with Medicare coverage, drug-plan options and billing questions. Counselors do not sell insurance. Use the provider page to arrange counseling or call 831-655-1334. Confirm appointment options and bring your specific coverage questions. This post does not recommend a plan or promise savings.
evidence: Provider confirms no-cost unbiased counseling, coverage topics and no insurance sales; page lists the Monterey contact number.

title: Meals at your door.
message: Homebound? Ask Meals on Wheels about Peninsula delivery.
details: The program lists homebound seniors age 60+, veterans and adults with disabilities who have limited ability to shop or cook. Service covers the Peninsula, including Marina, Seaside and Carmel Valley. Meals have no required charge; contributions are voluntary. Use Sign Up for Meals or call 831-375-4454. Confirm eligibility, your address and a start date with staff.
evidence: Provider page confirms listed groups, delivery area, enrollment and voluntary contributions. Its no-waitlist claim is not repeated as a current capacity guarantee.

title: Meals for homebound seniors.
message: Salinas Valley delivery. Start with the Meals on Wheels intake.
details: This senior program serves homebound adults age 60+ who cannot shop or cook, including temporary needs after illness or injury. Its area extends from Pajaro and Aromas to San Ardo and Bradley. Begin through the website Sign Up intake. Contributions are voluntary. Confirm your address, meal arrangements and start date; delivery days differ by area.
evidence: Provider FAQ confirms senior eligibility, territory, intake and voluntary contributions. Do not confuse this program with the separately priced non-senior HANDS program.

title: 60+ and need legal help?
message: No-cost services for Monterey County seniors.
details: Monterey County residents age 60 or older can request help with housing, benefits, consumer problems, estate planning and elder abuse. The provider lists no-cost legal assistance and representation. Call 831-899-0492 or use Need Legal Help on its website to ask about intake. Case acceptance and appointment availability are determined by the provider.
evidence: Provider homepage confirms age 60+, Monterey County, no-cost assistance, listed legal topics and contact number.

title: Looking for childcare?
message: Find local options. Check openings directly with each provider.
details: For children ages 0–12, the resource page links MyChildCarePlan and the local Resource & Referral specialist at 831-757-0775. Search by location, age and schedule, or request a specialist appointment. Families must contact individual providers about open spaces or waitlists. Referral help does not mean childcare is free; ask about fees and subsidy eligibility.
evidence: County childcare resource page lists ages, search tool and local specialist, and explicitly says families must check openings themselves.

title: Tools for independence.
message: Explore disability equipment and support through CCCIL.
sourceName: Central Coast Center for Independent Living
details: CCCIL helps people with disabilities find assistive technology, services, training and potential funding. It also describes a Voice Options device-loan pathway for people who have difficulty speaking. Contact 831-757-2968 in Salinas or 831-462-8720 in Capitola to discuss your needs. Ask about eligibility, costs and device availability before applying; equipment is not guaranteed.
evidence: Provider service page confirms assistive-technology coordination, funding referrals and Voice Options; homepage confirms the three-county service area.

title: Your next job starts here.
message: Free job-search help from Monterey County Works.
details: America’s Job Center staff can help with career planning, resume tools, workshops and training pathways. The provider lists these job-seeker services at no cost. Call 831-796-3331 or use the job-seeker page to get started. Ask which programs fit your situation and whether registration or an appointment is required; this is not a job offer.
evidence: Workforce Development Board page lists no-cost services, accessibility support and its contact number.

title: Need food nearby?
message: Santa Cruz County: call 831-662-0991 for food resources.
sourceName: Second Harvest Food Bank Santa Cruz County
details: Second Harvest directs people seeking food to its Community Food Hotline and food locator. Call 831-662-0991 or follow the food-access link on its official page. Ask about a distribution near your city and confirm its hours, requirements and current supply before traveling. This is a referral route, not a promise of food at a particular site.
evidence: Provider contact page explicitly identifies 831-662-0991 as the food-access number; a conflicting number on another site was excluded.

title: CalFresh paperwork?
message: Get application help from Second Harvest.
sourceName: Second Harvest Food Bank Santa Cruz County
details: Santa Cruz County residents can use the provider’s interest form or call 831-662-0991 to request help from its CalFresh outreach team. The interest form is a request for assistance, not an approved benefits application. Ask the team about current eligibility and required documents. Older income tables and immigration-category summaries are not reproduced here.
evidence: Provider page confirms outreach form and phone; no benefit amount, current legal eligibility rule or approval timeline is asserted.

title: Need diapers?
message: Find Santa Cruz County pickup options through Second Harvest.
sourceName: Second Harvest Food Bank Santa Cruz County
details: The provider lists community organizations that distribute diapers to the public and a separate list for enrolled program participants. Start with the public-distribution list, then contact the organization to check sizes, supply, hours and any requirements. Not every partner serves walk-ins, and this card does not confirm stock today.
evidence: Provider page distinguishes public distribution partners from enrolled-client programs; page carries an August 10, 2026 update date.

title: Unpaid wages? Get guidance.
message: Explore free legal help through Watsonville Law Center.
details: The center offers free legal services for low-wage people and families, including wage and workplace issues. Read the Contact page before seeking help: most services require appointments and capacity is limited. Participants in its partner healthcare or CalWORKs programs can ask their provider or caseworker for a referral. The business-inquiry phone is not an intake line, and the current-client line is not offered here for new clients.
evidence: Services and https://www.watsonvillelawcenter.org/contact/ reviewed together. Contact restrictions and limited capacity retained; no representation or response promised.

title: A rental housing problem?
message: Ask ECHO about repairs, rent concerns or housing disputes.
details: ECHO lists tenant/landlord information, mediation and legal-service referrals for Monterey County residents. Call its county line, 831-566-0824, to ask about the right service and current appointment options. The program page lists offices in several cities; confirm visits first. Counseling is not a promise of an attorney or rent payment.
evidence: Provider confirms county service area, topics, referrals and county number. Older dated office schedules are not promoted as current walk-in hours.

title: Keep your pet fed.
message: Free pet food through SPCA Monterey County.
details: For people in critical need of help feeding their pets. The provider lists Saturday pickup, 9:30–10:30 a.m., at 1002 Monterey-Salinas Highway; follow its directions past the Adoption Center. Call 831-373-2631 to confirm before traveling. Listed limits include one bag per order and two families per car. Food types and other supplies depend on donations.
evidence: Provider recipient section checked separately from donation hours. Saturday pickup, address, phone, limits and donation-dependent supply confirmed.

title: Caregivers need support too.
message: Talk with Del Mar about counseling, support and respite.
details: For people caring for a family member with memory impairment or a neurological condition that began after age 18 in the three-county service area. Call 800-624-8304 or request services through CareNav. The provider lists counseling, education and support at no cost; respite may have a sliding-scale copay and depends on funding and eligibility. Confirm which services fit your situation.
evidence: Provider confirms caregiver eligibility, counties, access routes, no-cost services and respite cost/funding limits.

title: Need an accessible ride?
message: Ask MST about RIDES eligibility and advance reservations.
details: MST RIDES is shared transportation for eligible people whose disability prevents use of regular fixed-route buses. Eligibility and trip coverage require MST review; a disability alone does not establish eligibility. Service follows defined route corridors and operating hours. Use the official information/application page and confirm fares and booking requirements before planning a trip.
evidence: MST service page and mobility FAQ confirm disability-related eligibility, service corridors and advance reservations. No universal or same-day ride promise.

title: Build your reading skills.
message: Explore adult tutoring at Salinas Public Library.
details: The library lists individual adult tutoring for reading, writing, English-language learning and high-school-equivalency goals. Call 831-758-7916 or use the sign-up link to ask about support. The page lists a waitlist for individual tutoring, so a tutor or start date is not guaranteed. Ask about current sessions and any requirements.
evidence: Official page lists tutoring subjects, sign-up and phone, and explicitly notes a waitlist. Old news items and Chromebook-giveaway claims excluded.

title: Need help? Start here.
message: Call 211 for free, confidential local referrals.
details: Free, confidential resource referrals, 24 hours a day. Ask about food, childcare and other local services. Tell the specialist your city and what you need. A referral does not guarantee eligibility, funding or an appointment.
evidence: Provider page confirms free, confidential, round-the-clock referrals and multilingual access.

title: Learn your bus route.
message: Free travel training from MST.
details: Everyone is eligible for fixed-route travel training. It can include planning a trip and an accompanied bus ride. Contact MST through its inquiry form to arrange training; this is not a ride booking or a promise of an immediate session.
evidence: MST describes free training for individuals and groups, says everyone is eligible and provides an inquiry form.

title: Need a computer?
message: Salinas libraries offer guest passes. Ask at the desk.
details: The library lists up to two hours of computer use with a library card or a guest pass from the desk. Check branch hours before visiting. A workstation may not be immediately available; printing charges are separate.
evidence: Current provider page explicitly permits guest passes, unlike an older page that says a library card is required.

title: Free library Wi-Fi.
message: Connect at Salinas libraries. No card needed.
details: The library lists public Wi-Fi at all locations, including adjacent parking lots, daily from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Building hours differ. Check the library page for connection instructions and current access.
evidence: Provider page confirms free community Wi-Fi without a card and gives daily access hours.

title: Streetlight out?
message: Send a service request through Salinas Connect.
details: Salinas Police directs streetlight outages, graffiti, abandoned vehicles and barking-dog reports to Salinas Connect. Use the official page to reach the correct form. This is a non-emergency service channel, not a news tip submission.
evidence: Official department page lists the four report categories and links to Salinas Connect.

title: Check your bus.
message: Open MST alerts before you go.
details: Open the current service-alert page and its MST RealTime link before traveling. This card does not say that your route is running normally or that no alerts exist. Service information can change after this card is made.
evidence: Official service-alert page provides MST RealTime and trip-planning links. No live status is reproduced.

title: Food in Castroville.
message: Nov. 5 · 9–10 a.m. · Our Lady of Refuge
details: The Food Bank lists November 5, 2026, 9–10 a.m. at Our Lady of Refuge Catholic Church, 11140 Preston Street. Check with the Food Bank before traveling. This listing does not confirm stock, required documents or eligibility; those details need provider confirmation.
evidence: Checked the Castroville section dated 11/5/26. Ignored old holiday listings elsewhere on the same page.

title: Food in Carmel Valley.
message: Nov. 6 · 9–10 a.m. · St. Philip’s Lutheran Church
details: The Food Bank lists November 6, 2026, 9–10 a.m. at St. Philip’s Lutheran Church, 8065 Carmel Valley Road, serving seniors and the general public. Confirm the schedule before traveling. Stock and document requirements are not confirmed.
evidence: Checked the Carmel Valley section dated 11/6/26 and its general-public designation; not the separate senior site.
